subject.title: [Feature Request] Hook Chain Integrity Protection Against Message Tampering

question: What hook-chain security model should OpenClaw support for mutable plugin hooks: host-owned audit/provenance for current in-process plugins, integrity checks across a future isolated-plugin boundary, or per-hook permission gating first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing checksums, audit logs, or per-hook allowlists would encode a plugin trust boundary, audit-retention policy, and compatibility contract that current code and docs do not settle.

options.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
options.body: Document the threat model, redaction and retention rules, protected boundary, and compatibility plan before changing hook runner behavior or config.

options.title: Ship redacted audit first
options.body: Add host-owned audit events for modifying hooks while deferring checksum enforcement and per-hook allowlists.

options.title: Defer checksums to isolated plugins
options.body: Keep checksum enforcement blocked on isolated-plugin IPC work so integrity checks are designed around a real boundary.

recommendation.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
recommendation.body: Document the threat model, redaction and retention rules, protected boundary, and compatibility plan before changing hook runner behavior or config.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the clearest current-main and recent-history connection to the hook runner, typed hook policy, and plugin config surfaces that would carry this decision into implementation.
